title: The Right of Resistance and Early Constitutional Compacts

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Issued by King Andrew II in 1222, just seven years after the Magna Carta, the *Aranybulla* was Hungary's seminal charter of liberties (*szabadságlevél*). Its famous 31st article is read as granting the nobles (and bishops) a right of resistance (*jus resistendi*).

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: According to the clause, resistance against a king who broke the charter was not to count as treason (*hűtlenség*).
